title: Media Modality
description: Media modality is the type of media that is being used to represent the content.

title: Still Image
description: A single, self-contained visual representation with no temporal dimension.

title: Video
description: A time-ordered sequence of frames shown at a defined rate to produce the appearance of motion.

title: Audio
description: Sound represented as a signal, whether standing alone or carried within a video file.

title: Text
description: Linguistic content carried as a sequence of characters that is machine-readable (captions, titles, comments, etc.).

title: Forensic Goal & Task
description: Encompasses all high-level objectives and tasks involved in digital media forensics, from detecting alterations to identifying sources and verifying integrity.

title: Forgery & Manipulation Detection
description: Determining whether media has been altered from its original state.

title: Content Synthesis
description: Detecting manipulations that involve generating entirely new content within a piece of media.

title: Full Synthesis
description: Determining whether an entire item was generated by a model.

title: Removal / Inpainting
description: Determining whether a region was deleted and the resulting gap filled with plausible substitute content.

title: Deepfakes
description: Deepfakes are videos manipulated using deep learning (DL) technology so that a person could be shown saying things they never said.

title: Expression / Attribute Manipulation
description: Detecting alterations to a person's facial expressions or addition of new attributes like a sunglasses.

title: Lip-sync / Reenactment
description: Determining whether a subject's mouth movement or facial performance was re-synthesised to follow a chosen audio or driving track.

title: Face Swap
description: Determining whether one person's facial identity was substituted for another's in media depicting a real subject.

title: Generative Up-scaling
description: Detecting if an image's resolution was artificially increased using generative models, which might introduce misleading details.

title: Generative Expand
description: Using a generative model to extend the borders of an existing image, creating new content that continues the original scene, background, and objects.

title: Content Rearrangement
description: Detecting manipulations where existing parts of the media are moved, copied, or spliced.

title: Copy-move
description: Determining whether a region was duplicated to another location within the item under examination.

title: Splicing
description: Determining whether a region taken from a different source was inserted into the item under examination.

title: Cropping
description: Analyzing an image to determine if it has been cropped, potentially to remove exculpatory or contextual information.

title: Signal-level Post-processing
description: Detecting manipulations that affect the entire signal, such as compression, which can be used to hide other alterations.

title: Compression
description: Analyzing compression artifacts and levels to understand an image's history.

title: Resizing
description: Analyzing the resizing of an image

title: Color Correction
description: Analyzing the color correction of an image

title: Blurring
description: Analyzing the blurring of an image

title: Sharpening
description: Analyzing the sharpening of an image

title: File Structure Tampering
description: Analyzing the file's binary structure for evidence of manual or programmatic alteration.

title: Metadata Tempering
description: Detecting alterations to a file's metadata (e.g., EXIF data) to mislead an investigation.

title: Source Identification & Attribution
description: Determining what produced an item: which device captured it, which model generated it, or which actor created and disseminated it.

title: Device Source Identification
description: Identifying the hardware (e.g., camera, scanner) that created the media.

title: Generative Model Attribution
description: Identifying the specific AI model or architecture used to create synthetic media.

title: Fingerprint Attribution
description: Finding unique, subtle artifacts (fingerprints) left by a specific generative model.

title: Diffusion-based
description: Determining whether content was produced by a diffusion model, and which one.

title: GAN-based
description: Determining whether content was produced by a generative adversarial (GAN) model, and which one.

title: Flow-based
description: Determining whether content was produced by a generative model built on normalizing flows, and which one.

title: Model Watermark Detection
description: Detecting invisible watermarks embedded by AI models to indicate that the content is synthetic.

title: Creator & Campaign Attribution
description: Linking a piece of media to a specific person, group, or organized campaign.

title: Integrity & Provenance Verification
description: Verifying that a piece of media has not been tampered with and tracking its history or chain of custody.

title: Watermark Verification
description: Determining whether an ownership or authenticity mark is present, valid, and intact, and what it asserts about the item.

title: Provenance Analysis
description: Reconstructing the lifecycle of a digital asset, including its creation and all subsequent modifications.

title: Contextual Analysis
description: Determining whether an item is presented in a truthful context, consistent with its accompanying information, regardless of whether the item itself was altered.

title: Steganography
description: Detecting hidden data or messages concealed within a media file.

title: Evidentiary Features
description: The top-level category for all of evidence that can be extracted from digital media to perform forensic tasks.

title: Computational Features
description: Abstract mathematical representations extracted from raw signals through algorithmic processing, including embeddings, transforms, and learned features from neural networks.

title: Spatial Features
description: The technique examines the pixels in a single image or frame — their values and the relationships among them.

title: Texture Based
description: The technique measures local patterns and variations in a single image or frame, capturing how visual detail is distributed and organized across a region.

title: Gradient
description: Measures the rate of change in intensity of pixels in an image.

title: Co-occurrence Matrix
description: A method that captures how often pairs of pixel intensity values occur in spatial relation to each other

title: Local Binary Patterns LBP
description: A texture descriptor that encodes the local spatial structure of an image by comparing each pixel to its surrounding neighbors.

title: Entropy
description: A measure of the randomness or complexity of pixel values in a region.

title: Keypoint
description: Distinctive points in an image (e.g., corners, blobs) used for matching and tracking.

title: Color Based
description: Features derived from color distributions or relationships within an image or a single frame.

title: Color Histogram
description: A representation of the distribution of colors in an image or a single frame.

title: Color Filter Array Bayer
description: A pattern used in digital cameras to capture color information.

title: Color Differences
description: Features computed by measuring the difference in color values between adjacent pixels or regions.

title: Noise Based
description: Features that analyze the statistical or signal-level noise characteristics across an image or a single frame.

title: PRNU Noise
description: Photo-Response Non-Uniformity (PRNU) is a sensor-level noise pattern unique to each camera.

title: SRM Features
description: The technique uses a fixed set of filters (the Spatial Rich Model) to suppress most of the visible image content and expose the residual traces left behind, then measures those traces.

title: Frequency Features
description: Features extracted by transforming the image from the spatial domain to the frequency domain, typically using transforms like DCT or FFT, to capture periodic patterns, compression artifacts, or editing traces not easily visible in pixel space.

title: Discrete Cosine Transform DCT
description: The technique represents image data as a combination of cosine components at different spatial frequencies, capturing how much coarse versus fine variation is present. This kind of representation is also used in JPEG compression.

title: Discrete Fourier Transform DFT
description: The technique represents the signal as a spectrum of sinusoidal components, capturing which spatial or temporal frequencies are present, how strong they are, and their phase.

title: Discrete Wavelet Transform DWT
description: The technique operates on the image decomposed into bands of coarse and fine detail, where each band remains tied to the location in the image it came from.

title: Temporal Features
description: The technique looks across successive video frames or stretches of audio to measure how the content changes over time.

title: Optical Flow Field
description: The pattern of apparent motion of objects between two consecutive frames.

title: Linguistic Features
description: Features derived from the text content associated with media, such as captions, comments, or metadata.

title: Textual Features
description: The technique computes representations from character-encoded text accompanying the media.

title: Acoustic Features
description: The technique computes spectral, prosodic, or temporal representations from an audio waveform.

title: Mel-frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC)
description: The technique summarizes what a short piece of audio sounds like by measuring how much sound energy falls into different frequency ranges, scaled to roughly match how people hear. MFCCs are a widely used conventional feature representation in speech and audio processing.

title: Perceptual Evidence
description: Observable phenomena that can be seen, heard, or perceived by humans during forensic examination, even when computational tools enhance the analysis precision.

title: Metadata & File Structure
description: The technique examines the information a file records about itself and how the file is internally organized.

title: Compression Artifacts
description: The technique looks for visible distortions introduced by lossy compression.

title: Biometric Signals
description: Cues related to the unique biological and behavioral traits of an individual.

title: Movement
description: The technique reads a subject's motion over time.

title: Shape
description: Cues related to the geometric structure and form of facial features.

title: Color
description: Changes in skin tone or other color attributes that may indicate physiological responses.

title: Geometric Structural Inconsistency
description: Cues related to errors in the shape, structure, and spatial arrangement of objects.

title: Blending Boundary
description: The transition region between a manipulated area and its surrounding content in an image or video, where visual inconsistencies in texture, color, or edge smoothness may indicate manipulation.

title: Warping
description: Distortions in the background or surrounding areas caused by manipulation.

title: Violation Of Physics
description: Cues where the media depicts events or properties that contradict the laws of physics.

title: Lighting
description: The way light interacts with objects and surfaces in the scene.

title: Shadow
description: The dark areas created by an object blocking light.

title: Reflection
description: Reflected scene details visible on shiny surfaces (e.g. eyes, glass, metal, water).

title: Perspective
description: The representation of three-dimensional objects on a two-dimensional surface.

title: Temporal Inconsistency
description: Artifacts that occur or change over time in a video or audio stream.

title: Flickering Jitter
description: Rapid and inconsistent changes in brightness, color, or position.

title: Semantic Coherence
description: Refers to the logical and contextual consistency of objects and events within a scene over time.

title: Cross Modal Inconsistency
description: Contradictions between different modalities of media, such as audio, video, and text.

title: Audio-Visual
description: The technique compares the visual and audio channels for agreement in content or timing.

title: Visual-Textual
description: The technique compares depicted visual content against accompanying text for agreement.

title: Search & Analysis Scope
description: Defines the boundaries and focus of a forensic examination, specifying where and at what level of detail the analysis is conducted.

title: Spatial Scope
description: Defines the area or level of spatial detail being examined within a frame or image.

title: Global
description: The analysis covers the full media content without narrowing to any specific region.

title: Region of Interest
description: The analysis is concentrated on a specific, targeted area within the media.

title: Human
description: A specific type of ROI where the focus of the analysis is a human subject.

title: Face
description: The analysis concentrates on a subject's whole facial region.

title: Mouth
description: The analysis concentrates on the mouth region.

title: Eyes
description: The analysis concentrates on the eye region.

title: Ears
description: Analysis focused on the ear region.

title: Nose
description: Analysis focused on the nose region.

title: Jawline/Chin
description: Analysis focused on the jawline and chin area.

title: Body
description: The analysis is focused on the body of the human subject.

title: Object
description: The analysis is focused on a specific object within the media.

title: Background
description: The analysis is focused on the background of the media.

title: Temporal Scope
description: Defines the duration or portion of time being examined in a video or audio file.

title: Full-sequence
description: The analysis takes in the item's entire duration in a single operation.

title: Segment
description: The analysis considers a bounded window of frames, consecutive or interval-sampled, drawn from part of the item's duration.

title: Single Frame
description: The analysis considers a single frame in isolation, drawing on no information from neighboring frames.

title: File Structure Scope
description: Focuses on the file's metadata and structure rather than its visual or audible content. This can reveal information about the file's origin, history, and integrity.

title: Metadata
description: The analysis addresses the descriptive fields embedded within a file (EXIF, XMP, C2PA, etc.), separate from its visible content.

title: Header
description: The analysis of the file's header, which defines its type and structure.

title: Contextual Scope
description: The analysis addresses material accompanying an item rather than the item itself — titles, comments, or surrounding post content.
